correctness.rationale: Under the independent rate-one Poisson embedding, completion time M_n=max first arrival E_i has n exp(−M_n) -> Exp(1). Conditional on M_n=t and unique last index, its count is exactly 1; all other n−1 counts are independent Poisson(t) conditional on at least one. Thus each nested deficit indicator has p=q_j(t)=Σ_(r=1)^(j−1)t^r/r!/(e^t−1), and exact mean 1+(n−1)q_j, variance (n−1)q_j(1−q_j), covariance (n−1)q_i(1−q_j) for i<j. Since at t=log(n/w), (n−1)q_j~w(log n)^(j−1)/(j−1)! and off-diagonal covariances vanish under coordinatewise square-root scaling, the bounded triangular-array Lindeberg theorem yields independent conditional normals; compact-uniform w and Exp mixing yield the stable joint limit and independent W. The stopped martingale E[(K_n−nM_n)^2]=n E M_n=nH_n and q_j derivative O((log n)^(j−1)/n) imply observable S_n=K_n/n replaces M_n with centered errors o_P(1) even on unstudentized scales. Independent finite truncated-Poisson enumeration verified all stated nested-indicator covariance formulas for t=2,6,12,18 and index pairs (2,3),(2,5),(3,6). All-n CLT is analytical, not finite evidence.
residual_risks: Number J of siblings is fixed; no growing-index or unequal-probability CLT is claimed.
The compact-uniform conditional CLT and random-clock replacement are asymptotic analytical steps, not asserted as certified by numeric tests.

Long proves conditional Bernoulli noise negligible ONLY at the larger first-order a_n,j scale. Ilienko also establishes independent centered completion TIMES, a different observable. No direct implication was found; priority remains best of knowledge with occupancy-CLT literature risk.

value.rationale: The first-order sibling deficits share one exponential amplitude and so are perfectly correlated asymptotically. The sharp question what remains after centering by the actually observable completion index is statistically and mathematically natural; the answer exposes independent second-order Gaussian noise, a mixed-normal version and exact finite-size conditional decorrelation powers. This adds a useful fluctuation layer to the established first-order coupon collector theorem rather than recalculating first moments.

limitations: Fixed J and equal-probability coupon draws only.
Conditional covariance formulas exactly condition on auxiliary Poisson M_n; the final Gaussian statistics use observed K_n/n.
